title: Published host-service port is rejected after Docker DNAT despite --allow-host-service-ports
symptoms: Connection to a host-published service (for example Redis or PostgreSQL) through the host gateway is rejected or times out
The port is listed in --allow-host-service-ports but a connectivity check still fails
conditions: Host access is enabled and the service port is allowed for the AWF gateway
Docker translates the published port before the DOCKER-USER chain, so the filter sees the container address and port rather than the gateway tuple
Observed on Ubuntu 26.04 / Docker 29 runners; other Docker versions are unknown
A rejection of a port that is not allowed, or of a direct container address, is expected policy rather than this defect
rootCause: Gateway-destination ACCEPT rules matched the post-DNAT destination, so published-service traffic fell through to the default reject. Matching conntrack's original gateway IP and port restores access without allowing direct container destinations.

probe.expect: Confirm the checked-out source adds a conntrack DNAT rule scoped to the original gateway IP and allowed port; compare with the redacted operator port list without sending traffic or dumping environments.

action: Use source containing the original-gateway-tuple conntrack rule and re-run with the required ports in --allow-host-service-ports. Keep host access gateway-scoped and limited to the listed ports. A failure for a port outside the configured list is expected.
